text:
maria: Hey team — customer reporting intermittent 502s from /v1/embeddings in their bulk job. Happening ~10-20% of requests and mostly for sequences > 1024 tokens. They can reproduce locally but only with their prod bundle. Can we collect a minimal repro and a debug bundle?

josh: Got it. Can you ask for the request IDs and a minimal curl that reproduces? Also need the full response headers and any stack traces.

maria: Yep asked for: request_id, request_ts, full response body, response headers, and a curl that hits the same payload (header + body). I sent this template:```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":["...your text..."],"batch_size":8}'
```

kevin: I'll toss in tiny SDK snips customers can run quickly (python/js/go). Keep them minimal so they can paste into terminal.

maria: Please add a note to set env var to capture request-id header, e.g. `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1` so we log `x-request-id`. Also ask them to include `--trace` output for curl if they can.

josh: Here are short snippets I use for repro collection — they return headers + body:```
# Python (requests)
import os, requests
url = "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
body = {"model":"open-embed-1","input":["sample text repeated to hit >1024 tokens ..."],"batch_size":8}
r = requests.post(url, json=body, headers=headers)
print(r.status_code)
print(r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
print(r.text)
```

kevin: JS (node fetch) and Go too:```
// Node (fetch)
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async ()=>{
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({model:'open-embed-1', input:[Array(200).fill('token').join(' ')], batch_size:8})
  });
  console.log(res.status);
  console.log(res.headers.get('x-request-id'));
  console.log(await res.text());
})();

// Go (net/http)
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "encoding/json"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main(){
  url := "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings"
  body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]interface{}{"model":"open-embed-1","input":[]string{string(bytes.Repeat([]byte("a"),1200))},"batch_size":8})
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, bytes.NewBuffer(body))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, _ := client.Do(req)
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println(resp.Header.Get("x-request-id"))
}
```

maria: Great — I'll paste those back to the customer. Also asked them to attach a debug bundle (stderr, SDK logs, and the minimal curl output). Sent guide:```
1) Run the curl/snippet that reproduces and capture headers: `curl -i --trace-ascii debug.txt ...`
2) Collect SDK logs (set REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 and run)
3) Tar up `debug.txt`, `stderr.log`, and any `sdk.log` and upload to the ticket
```

josh: If we get the request-id, we can correlate in our logs: `grep 19678.* <prod-logs> | grep <request-id>` — look for ERROR frames around the same timestamp. Common failure for >1024 tokens is KV cache OOM on older quantized runtimes; worth checking model variant and quantization flag.

maria: Customer replied with one sample header/body and request id. Pasting sanitized snippet:```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-request-id: rq_3f7b9c2a
content-type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"upstream timeout","code":502,"trace":"trace-9a7b"}}
```

kevin: Good. I'll pull logs for `rq_3f7b9c2a` and share findings. If it's an OOM we may see `KVCacheAllocError` in runtime logs.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-2026 created and linked to thread.

maria: Thanks — I'll keep customer updated and request the debug bundle upload. If they can't run the full payload, ask for a smaller reproducer that still triggers 502 (e.g., 2 inputs with >=1024 tokens each). :thumbsup:
